value: deliver the Crown (Finn's lunchbox) to Finn at the schoolyard
quote: She handed me the flag like it was the map that mattered.

We stepped past Mr. Bennett; the hedge turned back into an ordinary wall of green. The King's Road slid into a narrow sidewalk and the school bell, a drum somewhere ahead, began its slow, patient sound.
The compass tugged at my zipper like a small, insistent talisman and the Crown of Crumbs sat heavy against my hip.

Mara squealed and hugged my arm before I could be all noble about it, and the compass bumped my zipper like a polite reminder.

I took a breath. "It's not a knight's deed this time, sir," I said. The words surprised me by how steady they sounded. "It's a promise. Finn's seven. He'll wait all morning if he has to. I won't make him."
I put one foot on the good plank, kept my weight off the left-middle board, and edged across, the rope rubbing into my palms.
I grabbed the short coil of rope from the basket.
I had the Crown of Crumbs hugged to my side and the helmet shoved back so I could see, and for a second the moat felt very real.
Mara moved to the bank and made soft noises to Goliath, who watched us with the patience of a dog considering a puzzle.
When I reached the far side and set the Crown of Crumbs down, my hands ached and felt proud for being honest about how scared I was.
We stumbled into the schoolyard with five minutes left before the bell.
I put my hand to the dented metal lid of the lunchbox as if to check it was still there, and the weight of it was the same; what had changed was what the weight meant.
For a moment after he left, the three of us stood in a small triangle: Mara with her helmet crooked, me with jam still faint on my palm...
